description: White-team remediation: a document vault encrypts with a home-made stream cipher (static MD5 keystream, MD5(ciphertext) as MAC, unsalted MD5 passwords, timing-unsafe comparisons). Build the replacement module (fresh nonce, PBKDF2-HMAC-SHA256 key, HMAC-SHA256 keystream chain, encrypt-then-MAC, salted PBKDF2 passwords), migrate the data files with reencrypt_all, keep the CLI working and document the legacy weaknesses. check.py proves by experiment that the attacks are closed and legitimate use still works.

criteria: vault/crypto.py replaces the legacy cipher with a per-record random nonce from secrets, a PBKDF2-HMAC-SHA256 derived key (at least 200000 rounds), an HMAC-SHA256 keystream chain and encrypt-then-MAC verified with hmac.compare_digest, passwords as salted PBKDF2 records; vault/vault.db and vault/users.db are migrated to format 0x02 through reencrypt_all, the CLI uses the new module and still works, report/remediation.md names the four legacy weaknesses with the legacy function that carries each and the number of migrated records; the gate, the legacy module, the plan, the rollout passwords and the frozen snapshot files are untouched.
